description: Run a what-if sweep over a financing decision. Holds a scenario fixed while sweeping one input (credit_score, down_payment_percent, or rate_shift_bps) across a from/to/step range, returning a grid of best_lender / best_apr / monthly_payment at each value plus any flip_points where the winning lender changes. Use this to show how rate eligibility or affordability changes with credit score, down payment, or a market rate shift.

down_payment_percent.description: Baseline down payment percent (used unless swept).

sweep.description: The input to sweep and its range.

field.description: Which input to vary across the grid.

name: simulate_decision

flip_points.description: Values of the swept input where the winning lender or recommended action changes. Empty means the outcome is stable across the whole sweep.

grid.description: One row per swept value, showing how the outcome changes.

best_apr.description: Best published APR in percent at this swept value, taken as published without any score adjustment.

best_lender.description: Best lender at this swept value. It often does not change, because published credit-union rates are rarely tiered by score.

estimated_tier_apr.description: APR in percent after applying a modeled credit-tier adjustment — an estimate of what this borrower would actually be offered, not a published rate.

estimated_tier_monthly_payment.description: Monthly payment in dollars at the tier-adjusted APR; this is the realistic figure to quote a borrower at this credit score.

monthly_payment.description: Monthly payment in dollars at best_apr.

value.description: The swept input's value for this row, e.g. a credit score of 700.

product_type.description: Loan or deposit category this result covers, e.g. 'mortgage', 'auto_loan', 'heloc', 'savings'.

state.description: Two-letter US state code the result is scoped to (e.g. 'CA'). Null means the result was not filtered by state.

sweep_field.description: The input that was varied across the grid, e.g. 'credit_score'.
